items.title: Random-victim removal in the reinsertion loop
items.spec: In the remove-and-reinsert loop of solve, replace the choice i = np.argmin(r2) with a uniformly random index i = rng.integers(n) so that any circle, not only the smallest, is removed and reinserted each step. Keep the same reinsertion (uniform random centre, r = 0), the same _optimise call, the same _repair, and the same accept-if-better rule. Nothing else changes.

items.title: Dual-annealing outer search over centres with SLSQP polish
items.spec: After the random-restart phase, use scipy.optimize.dual_annealing over the 2n centre coordinates in [0,1]^(2n), with the energy being the negative sum of greedily repaired radii for those centres (radii set by the pairwise and wall-distance maximum-feasible rule, computed in numpy). Give dual_annealing maxiter and seed=rng.integers(2**31) and stop it when the time budget is used up, using a callback or a fixed small maxiter that fits the remaining time. Polish the best centres found with _optimise and _repair, and keep the better of this and the restart best.

items.title: Gaussian-cluster initial centres for random restarts
items.spec: In _solve_once, replace the uniform random initial centres with a mixture of k = 3 to 5 Gaussian clusters: draw cluster centres uniformly in [0.2, 0.8]^2, then draw each of the n centres from a normal with standard deviation 0.15 around a randomly chosen cluster centre, and clip to [INIT_LOW, 1 - INIT_LOW]. Keep the radii initialisation at INIT_RADIUS and all other code unchanged. The point is to vary density across restarts rather than always sampling a flat distribution.

items.title: Phase-dependent SLSQP iteration cap
items.spec: Pass a separate iteration cap to _optimise. During the random-restart phase use MAX_ITER_RESTART = 60 so that many starts fit into the budget, and during the reinsertion loop use MAX_ITER_POLISH = 400 so that each polish converges. Add an argument maxiter to _optimise and forward it to the minimize options. Keep everything else the same.

items.title: Stagnation-triggered full restart with global elite memory
items.spec: In the reinsertion loop, count consecutive steps without improvement. If the count reaches 60, save the current packing into an elite list if it is the best seen, then start a fresh random restart with _solve_once and _repair, and continue reinsertion from that new packing. Keep the global best across all restarts as the returned result. This is an iterated local search with restarts triggered by stagnation rather than a fixed phase length.

items.title: Radius destroy-and-regrow kick
items.spec: As the perturbation in the reinsertion loop, pick a random 25 percent of circles and multiply their radii by 0.5 while keeping every centre fixed. Then run _optimise from that point with all centres and radii free, followed by _repair, and accept under the usual rule that the repaired sum must beat the incumbent. Use the same loop and time budget as the original code, and do not change the removal step.

items.title: Single-radius shrink repair
items.spec: In _repair, when the most-overlapping pair (i, j) is found, shrink only the larger of the two radii by the full overlap amount, instead of scaling both radii by the ratio d / (r_i + r_j). Clamp the result at zero. Keep the loop count of 50 and the final SHRINK subtraction. This keeps the smaller circle intact and may preserve more total radius.

items.title: Cyclic round-robin removal of each circle
items.spec: In the reinsertion loop, replace the choice of the smallest circle with a cyclic index: at step t, remove and reinsert circle t mod n, using the same uniform random reinsertion, _optimise, _repair, and accept-if-better rule. Each full pass of n steps then visits every circle exactly once, which makes coverage systematic rather than biased toward small radii.

items.title: Tangent-distance initial radii from nearest neighbours
items.spec: In _solve_once, after drawing the uniform random centres, set each initial radius to half of the distance to its nearest other centre, further capped at the distance to the nearest wall and at 0.2. Use these radii as the SLSQP starting point in place of the constant INIT_RADIUS. Leave the restart logic and repair step unchanged.

items.title: Neighbourhood-local reinsertion site
items.spec: In the reinsertion loop, instead of drawing the new centre of the removed circle uniformly over the square, pick a random remaining circle k, then draw the new centre uniformly in a disc of radius 0.15 around c[k], clipped to [0, 1]^2. Keep r = 0, the same _optimise, _repair, and accept rule. The move then stays in the same local region of the packing rather than jumping across it.

items.title: Exact LP radius polish after SLSQP
items.spec: After each _optimise call (and before _repair), fix the centres and solve the radius-only problem as a linear program with scipy.optimize.linprog (highs): maximise sum r subject to r_i + r_j <= d_ij for all pairs, r_i <= wall distance of centre i, r_i >= 0. Use the LP radii in place of SLSQP radii if they are valid and larger. This removes the slack left by SLSQP's loose tolerance and gives exactly tight radii, so _repair rarely has to shrink anything. Keep the rest of the pipeline unchanged.

items.title: Active-contact Newton polish
items.spec: After the final best packing is chosen, identify active constraints (pair gaps and wall gaps below 1e-7). Solve the KKT-style system by running a second SLSQP call from the best point with tight ftol=1e-15 and maxiter=500, using only the constraints for near-active pairs (gap < 0.05) plus all wall constraints. Accept the result only if it is valid after _repair and has a larger sum. Use the last 5 percent of the time budget for this.

items.title: Rattler relocation move
items.spec: In the remove-and-reinsert loop, with probability 0.3 pick a circle that has fewer than 3 contacts (gap < 1e-6 to other circles or walls, a rattler) instead of the smallest circle, and reinsert it at a random position with radius 0. Otherwise keep the smallest-circle rule. Compute contacts with a vectorised distance matrix. Accept only improvements, as now.

items.title: Localised region destroy-and-rebuild
items.spec: In the reinsertion loop, pick a random point in the square, take the 3 circles whose centres are nearest to it, and re-seed all 3 at random positions inside the disc of radius 0.15 around that point with radius 0. Then run _optimise from there and accept if the repaired sum improves. This operates on a local cluster and gives a different neighbourhood from single-circle reinsertion.

items.title: Threshold accepting in reinsertion
items.spec: In the reinsertion loop, accept a candidate if its sum is at least the current sum minus a threshold that decays linearly from 0.004 to 0 over the loop's time. Keep a separate record of the best packing seen and return it at the end. This is deterministic threshold accepting and differs from the Metropolis rule already tried, because it uses a time-decaying cap and has no probability.

items.title: Move-limited SLSQP after reinsertion
items.spec: In the reinsertion loop, pass bounds to SLSQP: each centre may move at most 0.1 from its current value, and radii are in [0, 0.5]. The reinserted circle gets full bounds [0,1]. The smaller feasible box makes each solve converge faster and so gives more reinsertion steps in the same budget. Implement by adding an optional bounds argument to _optimise.

items.title: Solve n+1 then delete the smallest
items.spec: In the reinsertion phase, build the elite packing, then insert one extra circle at the largest hole (best of 300 random points by distance to the nearest circle edge) with radius 0. Run SLSQP on n+1 circles. Delete the smallest circle and run SLSQP on the remaining n circles to re-expand the others. Accept if the repaired sum improves. Make _optimise accept any circle count.

items.title: Round-robin over top-3 elites
items.spec: At the end of the restart phase keep the top 3 distinct packings by sum. In the reinsertion loop cycle through the 3 elites, applying the remove-and-reinsert step to each in turn and replacing that elite only on improvement. Return the best at the end. This spreads the search across several basins at no extra cost per step.

items.title: Adaptive removal choice by radius weights
items.spec: In the reinsertion loop, choose the circle to remove at random with probability proportional to 1/(r_i+0.01)^2 instead of always the smallest, so that the 2nd and 3rd smallest circles are also tried. Reinsert at a random uniform position with radius 0. Everything else stays as is.

items.title: Two-stage loose-then-tight SLSQP
items.spec: Change _optimise to run SLSQP first with maxiter=60 and ftol=1e-6, and then continue from that point with maxiter=200 and ftol=1e-9 only if the loose sum of radii (after clipping) is within 0.01 of the current best sum. Weak restarts are then dropped cheaply, so more restarts and reinsertion steps fit in the time budget. Pass the current best sum as an optional argument.

items.title: Combine analytic Jacobians with annealed acceptance
items.spec: Make two changes to the incumbent. (1) In _optimise, give SLSQP an analytic objective gradient (jac = 0 for the centres, -1 for the radii) and an analytic constraint Jacobian. For the pair rows, use d/dc_i = (c_i-c_j)/dist, d/dc_j = -that, and -1 for r_i and r_j. Use a floor of 1e-12 on dist. The wall rows and the r>=0 rows are fixed ±1 entries. Build the Jacobian as a dense (m, 3n) array, with the index arrays computed once per call. (2) In the remove-and-reinsert loop, accept a candidate whose sum is lower with probability exp((s2 - s)/T). T starts at 0.003 and falls linearly to 0 by the end of the budget. Draw the probability from rng. Always keep a separate best-ever (c, r) and return it. Every returned packing still goes through _repair.

items.title: LHS starts plus annealed reinsertion acceptance
items.spec: Combine the two replicated near-winners. In _solve_once, build the initial centres as a Latin hypercube sample in [0.1, 0.9]^2. For each axis, take rng.permutation(n), add rng.uniform(0, 1, n), divide by n, then map to [0.1, 0.9]. In the remove-and-reinsert loop, accept a worse candidate with probability exp((s2 - s)/T), with T falling linearly from 0.003 to 0 over the reinsertion phase. Track the best-ever repaired packing separately and return it. Change nothing else.

items.title: Rank-weighted choice of the circle to remove
items.spec: In the remove-and-reinsert loop, do not always remove argmin(r). Sort the circles by radius and pick one of the 6 smallest at random, with probability proportional to 1/(rank+1). Use rng for the draw. Then do what the code does now: set its centre uniformly at random, set its radius to 0, re-solve, repair, and accept only if the sum improves. The aim is to stop the loop from failing on the same circle over and over once the smallest circle is already well placed.

items.title: Shorter restart phase, longer reinsertion phase
items.spec: Change RESTART_FRACTION from 0.3 to 0.15, so that more of the 24 s budget goes to the remove-and-reinsert loop. That loop is where the incumbent gains most. Keep the guard that at least one restart runs. Change nothing else. This is a one-line schedule change that should be replicated twice.

items.title: Mini reinsertion polish inside each restart
items.spec: In the random-restart phase, after each restart's SLSQP solve and repair, run 3 remove-smallest-and-reinsert steps on that packing straight away. Reuse the same code as the main loop (factor it into a helper _reinsert_step(c, r, rng) that returns the better of old and new). Only then compare the result with best. This ranks restarts by their quality after a little refinement rather than as raw output, so promising basins are not thrown away early. Keep RESTART_FRACTION at 0.3, and the main reinsertion loop continues from the chosen best.

items.title: Corner and wall-biased reinsertion sites
items.spec: In the remove-and-reinsert loop, choose the new centre of the removed circle as follows. With probability 1/3, use a random corner offset by uniform(0.01, 0.08) on each axis toward the inside. With probability 1/3, use a random wall position: one coordinate is uniform(0.02, 0.98) and the other is uniform(0.01, 0.06) from a randomly chosen wall. Otherwise use a uniform point, as now. Use rng for every draw. Small circles in the best packings often sit in corner and wall gaps, which uniform sampling rarely hits.

items.title: Shrink-a-neighbour radius transfer move
items.spec: Add a second move to the remove-and-reinsert loop, used with probability 0.5. Pick a random circle j among the 10 largest. Set r[j] to 0.6*r[j]. Set the smallest circle's centre to c[j] plus a random offset of length 0.7*r_old[j], and its radius to 0. Re-optimise with _optimise from this start, then clip, repair, and accept if the sum improves (as the existing move does). The other half of the time, do the existing random reinsertion. This opens space inside dense regions, which uniform reinsertion cannot do.

items.title: Final convergence polish of the returned packing
items.spec: After the remove-and-reinsert loop and before returning, run one more SLSQP from the best (c, r) with maxiter 1000 and options ftol=1e-12. Do this only if at least 1.5 s of the 30 s remains, measured from t0 with process_time. Clip, repair, and keep the result only if its repaired sum is higher. This recovers the slack that the 200-iteration cap and the default ftol leave in the final packing, which the 1e-9 repair shrink cannot.

items.title: Reinsert with a small positive radius and jitter neighbours
items.spec: In the remove-and-reinsert loop, after choosing the random new centre p for the smallest circle, find all circles whose centres lie within 0.15 of p. Move each of them away from p by 0.01 along the line from p to its centre. Give the reinserted circle an initial radius of 0.01 instead of 0. Then run _optimise, clip, repair, and accept if the sum improves. Starting from a slightly infeasible point with an open pocket helps SLSQP actually grow the new circle, where a zero-radius circle tends to stay degenerate.

items.title: Two independent reinsertion chains with the time split
items.spec: After the restart phase, keep the two best distinct restart packings (sums that differ by more than 1e-4). Run the remove-and-reinsert loop on both in alternation, one step each per iteration, until half of the remaining budget is used. Then drop the weaker chain and spend the rest of the budget on the stronger one. Return the best repaired packing seen. If only one distinct packing exists, use the current behaviour. This hedges against committing early to a poor basin, and it is simpler than full round-robin over many elites.

items.title: Combine LHS starts, annealed acceptance and analytic Jacobians
items.spec: Apply three previously near-miss changes together on top of the current script. (a) In _solve_once, draw the initial centres as a Latin hypercube sample: for each of the two coordinates, take a random permutation of the n strata of [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW] and add uniform jitter inside each stratum. (b) In _optimise, pass analytic derivatives to SLSQP: the objective gradient is 0 for centre variables and -1 for radii; the constraint Jacobian is a dense (n(n-1)/2 + 5n, 3n) array with unit-vector entries (c_i-c_j)/d (d clamped to at least 1e-12) for pair rows, -1 for both radii in pair rows, +-1 and -1 for wall rows, and +1 for the r>=0 rows. (c) In the remove-and-reinsert loop, keep a separate current packing and best packing; accept a worse candidate into current with probability exp(delta/T), where T decays linearly from 0.002 to 0 over the remaining time budget; always return best. Keep _repair and all else unchanged.

items.title: Escalating removal rank after failed reinsertions
items.spec: In the remove-and-reinsert loop, keep an integer k starting at 0. At each step remove the circle with the (k mod n)-th smallest radius (np.argsort(r)[k % n]) instead of always the smallest, reinsert it at a uniform random position with radius 0 and re-solve as now. If the candidate improves the sum of radii, accept it and reset k to 0. Otherwise, increment a failure counter; after every 3 consecutive failures at the same rank, increase k by 1 and reset the counter. This makes the loop move on to larger circles when the smallest one is stuck. Everything else unchanged.

items.title: Shorten the random-restart phase to 10 percent
items.spec: Change RESTART_FRACTION from 0.3 to 0.1, so about 2.4 s goes to random SLSQP restarts and about 21.6 s goes to the remove-and-reinsert loop, which was the source of the only accepted gain. No other change. The 'or best is None' guard in the first while loop stays, so at least one restart always completes.

items.title: Short SLSQP solves in the reinsertion loop, full polish at the end
items.spec: Give _optimise an optional maxiter argument defaulting to MAX_ITER. In the remove-and-reinsert loop call it with maxiter=50, since the warm start is near a local optimum and most steps fail; this gives about three to four times more reinsertion attempts. End the loop at 0.9 of the budget rather than at the full budget, then run one final _optimise on the best packing with maxiter=400, clip and repair it, and keep it only if its repaired sum of radii is larger than the unpolished one. The random-restart phase keeps MAX_ITER = 200.

items.title: Local-subproblem SLSQP for each reinsertion
items.spec: Add a helper _optimise_local(n, c, r, idx) that runs SLSQP only over the centres and radii of the circles in idx (the reinserted circle plus its 8 nearest circles by centre distance to the new position), with all other circles held fixed. Constraints: pair non-overlap among the free circles, non-overlap of each free circle with each fixed circle, walls and r>=0 for the free circles; objective is minus the sum of free radii; maxiter 100. In the reinsertion loop, use this local solve for each step (it has 27 variables instead of 78, so it is several times faster), repair the result, and accept if the total sum improves. After every accepted step, and in any case every 20 steps, run the existing full _optimise on the current packing to let the improvement propagate, with the usual repair and accept-if-better check.

items.title: Variance-penalised objective in the first pass of each restart
items.spec: In _solve_once, run two SLSQP solves instead of one. The first, with maxiter 80, minimises -sum(r) + LAMBDA * n * var(r) with LAMBDA = 0.5 under the same constraints, which discourages solutions with a few tiny circles squeezed among large ones. The second is the existing _optimise call (true objective, MAX_ITER iterations) warm-started from the first result. Implement by giving _optimise an optional lam argument (default 0) and maxiter argument. The reinsertion loop keeps using the true objective only.

items.title: Late-acceptance hill climbing in the reinsertion loop
items.spec: Replace the strict-improvement acceptance in the remove-and-reinsert loop with late-acceptance hill climbing. Keep a circular history list of length L = 10 initialised with the current sum of radii, a current packing and a separate best packing. At step k, accept the repaired candidate into current if its sum is at least the current sum or at least history[k % L]; then set history[k % L] to the current sum. Update best whenever current exceeds it and return best at the end. This needs no temperature parameter and lets the search walk across plateaus and through slightly worse packings.

items.title: Split-the-largest move alternating with reinsertion
items.spec: In the remove-and-reinsert loop, on every second step use a split move instead of a uniform random reinsertion. Take the smallest circle i (as now) and the circle j chosen uniformly among the 5 largest. Draw a random angle theta; set the centre of j to c_j + 0.5*r_j*(cos theta, sin theta) and the centre of i to c_j - 0.5*r_j*(cos theta, sin theta), with both radii set to 0.45*r_j. Then run _optimise from this point, clip, repair and accept if the sum improves, exactly as for the other steps. This redistributes area from an oversized circle into the removed one, a topology change that a random reinsertion at radius 0 rarely achieves.

items.title: Reflection flip move across a contact pair
items.spec: Add a second move type to the reinsertion loop, used with probability 0.5. Pick a random circle i among the 8 smallest. Find its two nearest neighbours a and b by gap (centre distance minus the two radii). Reflect the centre of i across the straight line through the centres of a and b, so that it lands in the pocket on the other side of that pair; clip the new centre to [0.01, 0.99] and set r_i to 0. Then call _optimise, clip, repair and accept if the sum improves, as now. With the other probability 0.5 keep the existing remove-smallest uniform reinsertion. Use rng for all random choices.

items.title: Slack warm start for reinsertion solves
items.spec: In the remove-and-reinsert loop, before calling _optimise on the candidate, multiply all radii of the other n-1 circles by a factor drawn uniformly from [0.85, 0.97] (the reinserted circle keeps radius 0). This starts SLSQP from a strictly interior point with free room around every circle, so its first steps can rearrange centres instead of being pinned by the active contact set of the current jammed packing. The acceptance test still compares the repaired candidate sum against the unscaled current sum. No other change.
